title: Nā hana leʻaleʻa
description: Ten short stories about free time and hobbies in Hawaiʻi: surfing, a book club, a retired man's week, drawing, a ball game, cooking for the market, hiking, gardening, a voyaging canoe and family history.

lessons.title: Ka heʻe nalu ʻana o Kawena
lessons.summary: Kawena surfs at Haleʻiwa; on a winter day surfing there is forbidden because of the huge waves, so she drives to the calm south shore of Oʻahu.
lessons.text:
He wahine ʻōpio ʻo Kawena. Noho ʻo ia ma Haleʻiwa, ma ka ʻaoʻao ʻākau o Oʻahu. Mākaukau loa ʻo ia i ka heʻe nalu.

I ke kauwela, mālie ke kai ma Haleʻiwa. He mau nalu iki wale nō, a mahana ka wai. Pāʻani nā keiki iki ma ke kai mālie.

I ka hoʻoilo, nui loa nā nalu, a ʻaʻole mahana loa ka wai. I kekahi lā o ka hoʻoilo, ua hele ʻo Kawena i ke kahakai me kona papa heʻe nalu. Akā, ua pāpā ʻia ka heʻe nalu i kēlā lā. "Nui loa nā nalu," wahi a kekahi kanaka mālama kahakai. "Ua pāpā ʻia ka heʻe nalu i kēia lā."

Ua holo ʻo Kawena ma kona kaʻa i Waikīkī, ma ka ʻaoʻao hema o ka mokupuni. Ma laila, mālie ke kai a mahana ka wai, e like me ke kauwela. Ua heʻe ʻo ia i nā nalu iki no kekahi manawa lōʻihi.

Ma hope, ua hele wāwae ʻo ia ma ke one. Ua ʻike ʻo ia i nā kapuaʻi o nā keiki iki ma ke one. Ua ʻeha iki kona wāwae, no ka mea, ua kū ʻo ia ma luna o kekahi pōhaku i loko o ke kai. "Mākaukau au no nā nalu nui o Haleʻiwa i kekahi lā aʻe," wahi āna.

Nā nīnau:
Mākaukau ʻo Kawena i ka heʻe nalu?
ʻAe, mākaukau loa ʻo ia i ka heʻe nalu.
Mahana ka wai ma Haleʻiwa i ke kauwela?
ʻAe, i ke kauwela, mālie ke kai a mahana ka wai.
Ua pāpā ʻia ka heʻe nalu ma Haleʻiwa i kekahi lā o ka hoʻoilo?
ʻAe, ua pāpā ʻia ka heʻe nalu, no ka mea, nui loa nā nalu.
Ua ʻike ʻo Kawena i nā kapuaʻi o wai ma ke one?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i nā kapuaʻi o nā keiki iki.
Ua ʻeha kona wāwae?
ʻAe, ua ʻeha iki kona wāwae.

lessons.title: Ka hui heluhelu
lessons.summary: Leimomi's book club in Kailua reads a long story; Kahealani does not understand one chapter, Leimomi compares the book with another one, and the group argues about the ending.
lessons.text:
I kēlā me kēia mahina, hui ʻo Leimomi me kona mau hoaaloha ma kona hale ma Kailua. He hui heluhelu kā lākou. Heluhelu lākou i nā puke o ka moʻokalaleo Hawaiʻi, a kamaʻilio lākou no ka puke. Aloha nui ʻo Leimomi i ka moʻokalaleo.

I kēia mahina, ua heluhelu lākou i kekahi puke moʻolelo kahiko. He 20 mokuna o ka puke. Ua heluhelu kēlā me kēia kanaka i nā mokuna a pau ma ka hale.

Ma ka hui, ua ʻōlelo ʻo Kahealani: "ʻAʻole maopopo iaʻu ka mokuna 15." Ua heluhelu hou ʻo Leimomi i ka mokuna 15 no ka hui.

A laila, ua hoʻohālikelike ʻo Leimomi i kēia puke me ka puke o ka mahina i hala. "Ma nā puke ʻelua, hele kekahi kaikamahine i ka mauna e ʻimi i kona makuakāne," wahi āna. "He laʻana kēia. Ma kēia laʻana, hiki iā ʻoe ke hoʻohālikelike i nā puke ʻelua." ʻĀnō, ua maopopo iā Kahealani ka mokuna.

Ma hope, ua hoʻopaʻapaʻa ka hui no ka hopena o ka puke. Ua manaʻo ka hapanui, he hopena maikaʻi. Akā ua manaʻo ʻo Kahealani, he hopena kupanaha. "Kupanaha loa!" wahi āna. Ua hoʻopaʻapaʻa lākou no kekahi manawa lōʻihi, akā me ke aloha.

I ka pau ʻana, ua koho ka hui: he puke mele aiʻole he puke moʻolelo hou? Ua koho ka hapanui i ka puke moʻolelo hou.

Nā nīnau:
Heluhelu ka hui i nā puke o ka moʻokalaleo Hawaiʻi?
ʻAe, heluhelu lākou i nā puke o ka moʻokalaleo Hawaiʻi.
ʻEhia mokuna o ka puke?
He 20 mokuna o ka puke.
Ua maopopo iā Kahealani ka mokuna 15?
ʻAʻole, ʻaʻole i maopopo iā ia ma mua.
Ua hoʻohālikelike ʻo Leimomi i kēia puke me ka puke hea?
Ua hoʻohālikelike ʻo ia me ka puke o ka mahina i hala.
He puke mele aiʻole he puke moʻolelo ka puke hou?
He puke moʻolelo ka puke hou.

lessons.title: Ka pule a Kanaʻina
lessons.summary: Kanaʻina, retired in Lāʻie, has a hobby for every day of the week, and tells his daughter about it on the phone.
lessons.text:
He 68 makahiki ʻo Kanaʻina. ʻAʻole ʻo ia e hana hou ana. Noho ʻo ia me kāna wahine ʻo Lahela ma Lāʻie, ma Oʻahu. He nohona hou ko Kanaʻina: he hana leʻaleʻa kāna no kēlā me kēia lā o ka pule.

Ma ka Pōʻakahi, hīmeni ʻo ia me kekahi hui ma ka hale pule. Ma ka Pōʻalua, kanu ʻo ia i nā pua ma mua o kona hale. Ma ka Pōʻakolu, heluhelu ʻo ia i nā puke ma ka hale waihona puke. Ma ka Pōʻahā, aʻo ʻo ia i nā keiki o ke kaiāulu i ka hula kahiko. Ma ka Pōʻalima, holo waʻa ʻo ia me kona mau hoaaloha.

Ma ka Pōʻaono, hoʻāla ʻo Kanaʻina iā Lahela ma mua o ka puka ʻana o ka lā, a hele lāua i ke kahakai. ʻAʻole makemake ʻo Lahela e ala ma mua o ka lā, akā hoʻāla mau ʻo Kanaʻina iā ia. Ma ka Lāpule, hele lāua i ka hale pule.

I kekahi lā, ua kelepona mai kā lāua kaikamahine. "Pehea ko ʻolua nohona?" wahi āna. "ʻOia mau nō," wahi a Kanaʻina. "Hīmeni au ma ka Pōʻakahi, kanu au i nā pua ma ka Pōʻalua, heluhelu au ma ka Pōʻakolu, hula au ma ka Pōʻahā, a holo waʻa au ma ka Pōʻalima. A ma ka Pōʻaono, hoʻāla au i kou makuahine!" Ua ʻōlelo ʻo Lahela: "ʻOia mau nō kēia kanaka!"

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana a Kanaʻina ma ka Pōʻakolu?
Heluhelu ʻo ia i nā puke ma ka Pōʻakolu.
Hoʻāla ʻo wai iā Lahela ma ka Pōʻaono?
Hoʻāla ʻo Kanaʻina iā Lahela ma ka Pōʻaono.
Hele lāua i hea ma ka Lāpule?
Hele lāua i ka hale pule ma ka Lāpule.
He nohona maikaʻi ko Kanaʻina a me Lahela?
ʻAe, he nohona maikaʻi ko lāua.

lessons.title: Ke kahakiʻi ʻana o Kaleihua
lessons.summary: Kaleihua, a twelve-year-old girl in Makawao, loves drawing; she starts with simple shapes, gets a digital drawing tablet, and her teacher encourages her to enter a contest.
lessons.text:
He 12 makahiki ʻo Kaleihua. Noho ʻo ia ma Makawao, ma Maui. Makemake nui ʻo ia e kahakiʻi. Kahakiʻi ʻo ia i kēlā me kēia lā ma hope o ke kula.

Ua hoʻomaka ʻo ia me nā kiʻi maʻalahi. "E kahakiʻi mua i ka pōʻai a me ke kuea," wahi a kona kumu, ʻo Kaʻōpua. "Ma hope, e kahakiʻi i ka pelamika."

ʻĀnō, kahakiʻi ʻo ia i nā pua a me nā manu. I kēia lā, ua kahakiʻi ʻo ia i kekahi manu me nā hulu ʻulaʻula ma luna o kekahi lau nui o ka maiʻa. Ua kahakiʻi ʻo ia i kēlā me kēia hulu o ka manu.

Ua hāʻawi kona kupuna wahine iā ia i kāna mau lako kahakiʻi kahiko. Ma kona lā hānau, ua loaʻa iā ia kekahi lako hou: he papa kikohoʻe. Hiki iā ia ke kahakiʻi ma ka papa kikohoʻe, a hoʻouna i kāna mau kiʻi i kona kupuna wahine.

He kanaka kahakiʻi kāʻeʻaʻeʻa ʻo Kaʻōpua. Ua nānā ʻo ia i nā kiʻi o Kaleihua. "Kāʻeʻaʻeʻa ʻoe! E kahakiʻi mau!" wahi āna. Ua paipai ʻo ia iā Kaleihua e komo i kekahi hoʻokūkū kahakiʻi. Ua komo ʻo Kaleihua me kāna kiʻi o ka manu a me ka lau, a ua lanakila ʻo ia.

Nā nīnau:
Kahakiʻi ʻo Kaleihua i kēlā me kēia lā?
ʻAe, kahakiʻi ʻo ia i kēlā me kēia lā ma hope o ke kula.
He aha nā kiʻi mua a Kaleihua?
ʻO ka pōʻai, ke kuea a me ka pelamika.
He aha ka lako hou a Kaleihua?
He papa kikohoʻe kāna lako hou.
Ua paipai ʻo Kaʻōpua iā Kaleihua?
ʻAe, ua paipai ʻo ia iā ia e komo i ka hoʻokūkū.

lessons.title: Ke kinipōpō a Keoki
lessons.summary: Nine-year-old Keoki plays a ball game in Kapolei; his older brother teases him, he loses a baby tooth when the ball hits his mouth, and he later helps his team win.
lessons.text:
He 9 makahiki ʻo Keoki. Makemake nui ʻo ia i ka haʻuki. Pāʻani ʻo ia i ke kinipōpō me kekahi kime ma Kapolei. Ma kēia haʻuki, pīpeku nā keiki i ke kinipōpō me ko lākou wāwae. ʻAʻole lākou e lawe i ke kinipōpō me ka lima.

Ma ka hoʻomaʻamaʻa ʻana, helu ke kumu ʻo Kaluna: "ʻEkahi, ʻelua, ʻekolu!" a holo nā keiki. Ma ka helu ʻekahi, pīpeku ʻo Keoki i ke kinipōpō.

Ma mua, ʻaʻole maikaʻi ʻo Keoki ma ka pīpeku ʻana. Ua hoʻohenehene kona kaikuaʻana ʻo Iakoba iā ia: "Ua pīpeku hou ʻoe i ka lepo, ʻaʻole i ke kinipōpō!" ʻAʻole makemake ʻo Keoki i ka hoʻohenehene ʻana. "Mai hoʻohenehene i kou kaikaina," wahi a Kaluna iā Iakoba. "ʻAʻole pēlā ke kaikuaʻana maikaʻi. Ke holomua nei ʻo Keoki i kēlā me kēia pule."

I kekahi hoʻokūkū, ua hāʻule ʻo Keoki, a ua pā ke kinipōpō i kona waha. Ua ʻeha kona waha, a ua hemo kekahi niho. Ua lawe kona makuahine iā ia i ke kauka niho. "He niho keiki wale nō kēia," wahi a ke kauka. "E ulu ana kekahi niho hou ma kou waha."

Ma ka pule aʻe, ua pāʻani hou ʻo Keoki. Ua pīpeku ʻo ia i ke kinipōpō, a ua lanakila kona kime. "Pēlā nō, e Keoki!" wahi a Kaluna. Ua ʻōlelo ʻo Iakoba: "Ua holomua nui ʻoe!" ʻAʻole ʻo ia i hoʻohenehene hou i kona kaikaina.

Nā nīnau:
Pāʻani ʻo Keoki i ke kinipōpō ma Kapolei?
ʻAe, pāʻani ʻo ia me kekahi kime ma Kapolei.
Ua hoʻohenehene ʻo wai iā Keoki?
Ua hoʻohenehene kona kaikuaʻana ʻo Iakoba iā ia.
Ua hemo kekahi niho ma ka waha o Keoki?
ʻAe, ua hemo kekahi niho keiki.
He aha ka ʻōlelo a ke kauka?
"He niho keiki wale nō kēia," wahi a ke kauka.
Ua holomua ʻo Keoki?
ʻAe, ua holomua nui ʻo ia.

lessons.title: Ka pipi a Kahanu
lessons.summary: Kahanu loves to cook; he pays for a licence and a stall to sell his beef at the Saturday market in Kaimukī, meets a cook called Leialoha there and introduces her to his mother.
lessons.text:
Hana ʻo Kahanu ma kekahi keʻena ma Honolulu, akā ʻo ke kuke kāna hana leʻaleʻa. Kuke ʻo ia no kona ʻohana a me kona mau hoaaloha. ʻO ka pipi kāna ʻai kaulana. "E kūʻai aku ʻoe i kēia pipi ma ka mākeke!" wahi a kona mau hoaaloha.

Ua makemake ʻo Kahanu e kūʻai aku i kāna pipi ma ka mākeke o Kaimukī ma ka Pōʻaono. Akā, pono e loaʻa iā ia he laikini. ʻAʻole hiki ke kūʻai aku i ka ʻai ma ka mākeke me ka laikini ʻole. Ua hele ʻo ia i ke keʻena aupuni, a ua hoʻolilo ʻo ia i ʻelua haneli kālā no ka laikini.

Ua hoʻolilo pū ʻo ia i hoʻokahi haneli kālā no kekahi pākaukau a me nā mea kuke. Ma ka Pōʻaono, ua kau ʻo ia i ka pākaukau ma ka mākeke, a ua kuke ʻo ia i ka pipi ma laila.

Ua hele mai kekahi wahine i ka pākaukau. "E ʻoluʻolu, hoʻokahi pā pipi," wahi āna. ʻO Leialoha kona inoa, a he kuke ʻo ia ma kekahi hale ʻaina. Ua kamaʻilio lāua no ke kuke ʻana no kekahi manawa. ʻOluʻolu loa ʻo Leialoha.

Ma ka Pōʻaono aʻe, ua hele mai ka makuahine o Kahanu i ka mākeke. Ua hoʻolauna ʻo Kahanu iā Leialoha i kona makuahine: "ʻO kuʻu hoaaloha hou kēia, ʻo Leialoha. He kuke ʻo ia." Ua ʻōlelo ka makuahine: "Aloha ʻoe, e Leialoha! He kuke kuʻu keiki, a he kuke ʻoe!"

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana leʻaleʻa a Kahanu?
ʻO ke kuke kāna hana leʻaleʻa.
Ua hoʻolilo ʻo Kahanu i ʻehia kālā no ka laikini?
Ua hoʻolilo ʻo ia i ʻelua haneli kālā no ka laikini.
He wahine ʻoluʻolu ʻo Leialoha?
ʻAe, ʻoluʻolu loa ʻo Leialoha.
Ua hoʻolauna ʻo Kahanu iā Leialoha iā wai?
Ua hoʻolauna ʻo ia iā Leialoha i kona makuahine.

lessons.title: Ke alahele ma ka ululāʻau
lessons.summary: Kauakea and Nālani hike a forest trail near Kīlauea; they see a red bird and wild pigs, and a small earthquake drops a tree across the trail, so they go back another way.
lessons.text:
Makemake ʻo Kauakea lāua ʻo Nālani i ka hele wāwae ma nā alahele o ka mokupuni ʻo Hawaiʻi. I kēlā me kēia Lāpule, hele lāua ma kekahi alahele hou.

I kēia Lāpule, ua hele lāua ma kekahi alahele i loko o ka ululāʻau kokoke i Kīlauea. Ua hāpai ʻo Kauakea i ka wai, a ua hāpai ʻo Nālani i ka ʻai.

Maluhia loa ka ululāʻau. ʻAʻohe kanaka ʻē aʻe ma ke alahele. Lewa nā ao haʻahaʻa ma luna o nā lāʻau. Ua kuhi ʻo Nālani i kekahi manu ʻulaʻula ma luna o kekahi lāʻau. "E nānā!" wahi āna.

Ma hope, ua kuhi ʻo Kauakea i kekahi mau puaʻa hihiu ma ka ululāʻau. ʻEkolu puaʻa hihiu, he ʻeleʻele lākou. Ua holo nā puaʻa hihiu i loko o ka ululāʻau.

A laila, ua ōlaʻi. He ōlaʻi liʻiliʻi wale nō, akā ua hāʻule kekahi lāʻau nui ma luna o ke alahele. "Pōʻino!" wahi a Nālani. ʻAʻole hiki iā lāua ke hele hou ma ia alahele.

Ua hoʻi lāua ma kekahi alahele ʻē aʻe, ma kahi haʻahaʻa o ka mauna. ʻAʻole i ʻeha lāua. Ma laila, ua lewa hou nā ao ma luna o lāua. "He pōʻino ka ōlaʻi," wahi a Kauakea, "akā maluhia hou ka ululāʻau. He lā maikaʻi nō."

Nā nīnau:
Ua hele lāua ma kekahi alahele i loko o ka ululāʻau?
ʻAe, ua hele lāua ma kekahi alahele i loko o ka ululāʻau kokoke i Kīlauea.
Ua hāpai ʻo Nālani i ka wai?
ʻAʻole, ua hāpai ʻo Nālani i ka ʻai.
Lewa nā ao ma luna o nā lāʻau?
ʻAe, lewa nā ao haʻahaʻa ma luna o nā lāʻau.
Ua ʻike lāua i nā puaʻa hihiu?
ʻAe, ua holo ʻekolu puaʻa hihiu i loko o ka ululāʻau.
He aha ka pōʻino?
Ua ōlaʻi, a ua hāʻule kekahi lāʻau nui ma luna o ke alahele.

lessons.title: Ka ʻāina o Kaʻilikea
lessons.summary: Kaʻilikea, a university chemist, grows vegetables on a small community plot in Mānoa without chemicals, learns from an old farmer, and deals with a thief.
lessons.text:
He akeakamai ʻo Kaʻilikea ma ke kulanui ma Mānoa. Noiʻi ʻo ia i nā kemikala. Akā ma ka Pōʻaono a me ka Lāpule, mahiʻai ʻo ia ma kekahi ʻāina o ke kaiāulu.

He ʻāpana ʻāina liʻiliʻi kona: he 200 kapuaʻi kuea ka ʻalea. ʻAʻole nui ka ʻalea, akā kanu ʻo ia i nā mea kanu he nui ma laila.

Hoʻohana ʻo Kaʻilikea i nā kemikala ma kāna hana, akā ʻaʻole ma kona ʻāpana ʻāina. Ua nānā ʻo ia i ka lepo ma kona keʻena. "He nui nā kumumea maikaʻi i loko o ka lepo," wahi āna. "No nā kumumea, ʻaʻole pono nā kemikala."

Kūkā ʻo ia me kekahi mahiʻai kahiko, ʻo Pilipo. He mahiʻai ʻo Pilipo no 50 makahiki. Ua kūkā lāua no ke kanu ʻana. "E kanu ma nā laina pololei," wahi a Pilipo. Ua kanu ʻo Kaʻilikea ma nā laina pololei.

I kekahi pule, ua nalowale kekahi mau mea kanu. Ua ʻaihue ʻia lākou! Ua hoʻopilikia kekahi ʻaihue i nā mahiʻai o ke kaiāulu. Ua kūkā nā mahiʻai a pau, a ua kau lākou i kekahi pā. ʻAʻole i hoʻi hou mai ka ʻaihue, akā hoʻopilikia mau nā manu i nā mea kanu.

I ka pau ʻana o ka mahina, ua hōʻiliʻili ʻo Kaʻilikea i kāna mau mea kanu. Ua hoʻouka ʻo ia i nā pahu i kona kaʻa, a ua hoʻouka pū ʻo Pilipo i kekahi pahu.

Nā nīnau:
He akeakamai ʻo Kaʻilikea?
ʻAe, he akeakamai ʻo ia ma ke kulanui ma Mānoa.
He aha ka ʻalea o kona ʻāpana ʻāina?
He 200 kapuaʻi kuea ka ʻalea o kona ʻāpana.
Hoʻohana ʻo ia i nā kemikala ma kona ʻāpana ʻāina?
ʻAʻole, ʻaʻole ʻo ia e hoʻohana i nā kemikala ma laila.
Ua kūkā ʻo Kaʻilikea me wai?
Ua kūkā ʻo ia me ka mahiʻai kahiko ʻo Pilipo.
Ua ʻaihue ʻia kekahi mau mea kanu?
ʻAe, ua ʻaihue ʻia kekahi mau mea kanu.

lessons.title: Ka waʻa ma ke awa
lessons.summary: After work Keakealani helps look after a voyaging canoe at Honolulu harbour; she sails with it to North America and back, and the harbour holds a celebration for its return.
lessons.text:
Hana ʻo Keakealani ma kekahi waihona kālā ma Honolulu. Ma hope o ka hana, hele ʻo ia i ke awa o Honolulu e kōkua me kekahi waʻa holo moana. Mālama ʻo ia i ka waʻa ma ke awa.

I kēia makahiki, ua holo ka waʻa i ka ʻāinapuniʻole ʻo ʻAmelika ʻĀkau, a hoʻi mai. Ua holo pū ʻo Keakealani. ʻO Kamakana ke poʻo o ka waʻa. Ma ka moana, kauoha ʻo Kamakana i nā kānaka, a hana lākou e like me kāna kauoha.

I kekahi pō, ua hoʻoweliweli kekahi ʻino nui i ka waʻa. Ua pā ka makani ikaika, a nui loa nā nalu. Ua kauoha ʻo Kamakana: "E noho pū! E paʻa i ka waʻa!" Ua hoʻoweliweli ka ʻino i ka waʻa no ka pō a pau, akā i ka puka ʻana o ka lā, ua pau ka ʻino.

Kokoke i ka ʻāinapuniʻole, ua ʻike lākou i kekahi kanaka ma kekahi moku liʻiliʻi. Ua haki kona moku. Ua hoʻopakele lākou i ke kanaka, a ua lawe lākou iā ia i ka ʻāina.

Ma hope o ʻelua mahina, ua hoʻi mai ka waʻa i ke awa o Honolulu. He hoʻolauleʻa nui ma ke awa, me ka hula, ke mele a me ka ʻai. Ma mua o ka hoʻolauleʻa, ua pule kekahi kahu no ka waʻa. "E hīmeni kākou!" wahi a ke kahu. "He huakaʻi kupaianaha kēia," wahi a Kamakana. "Ua holo kākou i ka ʻāinapuniʻole, a ua hoʻi mai kākou. Kupaianaha!"

Nā nīnau:
Ua holo ka waʻa i ka ʻāinapuniʻole hea?
Ua holo ka waʻa i ka ʻāinapuniʻole ʻo ʻAmelika ʻĀkau.
Ua hoʻoweliweli ke aha i ka waʻa?
Ua hoʻoweliweli kekahi ʻino nui i ka waʻa.
Ua hoʻopakele lākou iā wai?
Ua hoʻopakele lākou i kekahi kanaka ma kekahi moku liʻiliʻi.
Aia ka hoʻolauleʻa ma hea?
Aia ka hoʻolauleʻa ma ke awa o Honolulu.

lessons.title: Ka inoa ma ka palapala
lessons.summary: Kaipolani's hobby is family history; she reads about the constitution of 1887, the queen's imprisonment and the petition of 1897, and finds her great-great-grandfather's name on it.
lessons.text:
ʻImi ʻo Kaipolani i ka moʻolelo o kona ʻohana. ʻO ia kāna hana leʻaleʻa. Heluhelu ʻo ia i nā palapala kahiko ma ka pūnaewele.

I ka makahiki 1887, ua koi kekahi hui haole i ka Mōʻī Kalākaua e kau inoa i kekahi kumukānāwai hou. Ua lilo ka mana o ke aupuni i ka poʻe haole.

I ka makahiki 1893, ua makemake ka Mōʻī Liliʻuokalani e hāʻawi i kekahi kumukānāwai hou i ka lāhui, akā ua lawe ka poʻe haole i ke aupuni. I ka makahiki 1895, ua lilo ʻo Liliʻuokalani i paʻahao ma ka hale aliʻi ʻo ʻIolani. He paʻahao ʻo ia ma laila no ʻewalu mahina.

I ka makahiki 1897, ua kau inoa nā kānaka Hawaiʻi he nui ma kekahi palapala kūʻē. Ua lawe ʻehā ʻelele i ka palapala i Wakinekona. Ua hele nā ʻelele i mua o nā luna o ke aupuni o ʻAmelika.

Ua heluhelu ʻo Kaipolani i nā inoa ma ka palapala, a ua ʻike ʻo ia i kekahi inoa: Kahikona! ʻO Kahikona ke kupuna o kona kupuna. Ua piha kona puʻuwai i ke aloha. "He kanaka kūpaʻa ʻo Kahikona," wahi āna. Ua kūpaʻa ʻo ia i kona mōʻī a me kona ʻāina.

Ua hōʻike ʻo Kaipolani i ka palapala i kāna keiki. "ʻOiaʻiʻo? Ua kau inoa ko kāua kupuna ma kēia palapala?" wahi a ke keiki. "ʻAe, he ʻoiaʻiʻo," wahi a Kaipolani. "ʻO kēia ko kāua hoʻoilina: ka puʻuwai kūpaʻa a me ke aloha ʻāina."

Nā nīnau:
Ua lilo ʻo wai i paʻahao i ka makahiki 1895?
Ua lilo ka Mōʻī Liliʻuokalani i paʻahao ma ka hale aliʻi ʻo ʻIolani.
Ua ʻike ʻo Kaipolani i ka inoa o wai ma ka palapala?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i ka inoa o Kahikona, ke kupuna o kona kupuna.
He aha ka hoʻoilina o Kaipolani?
ʻO ka puʻuwai kūpaʻa a me ke aloha ʻāina kona hoʻoilina.
